page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier for general compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1869.19 and a multi-core score of 7770.86. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 421.23 GB/sec, which drops to 60.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 43.15 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and AES. In application-level benchmarks, the instance handles 8.03 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 12.11 GB/sec. However, LLM inference performance on a medium 7B model is weak, generating 7.51 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7se.2xlarge offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring significant memory capacity without the need for high-performance local storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of local storage means users must rely on external network-attached storage. This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, data buffering, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.
